log: WHAT DOES ONE CHROMATIN MARK COST, AND DOES IT DEPEND ON WHICH MARK?
Displacement from a methyl falls ~15x within 15 A, so a mark should not need the whole
structure solved -- only a local region. How large that region must be IS the per-mark cost,
and it is measured here against the exact full-structure answer rather than assumed.
Marks are not interchangeable: 5mC is STERIC and neutral, acetylation REMOVES a +1 charge,
phosphorylation ADDS -2. A charge change was already shown to have a tail a steric change
does not have, so the prediction stated before running is that they will cost differently.
1KX5 no waters: 13625 atoms, 263765 springs. Same network as the propagation run, so the
numbers are directly comparable to it.
MARK SITES (chosen as the most buried of each type, so surroundings are comparable):
5mC on DC C5 atom 5093 | acetyl on LYS NZ atom 9037 | phospho on THR OG1 atom 6868
REGION SIZE NEEDED. Relative error over a FIXED 10 A set of atoms around the mark
(fixed, so every column answers the same question) against the EXACT full-structure solve.
Lower is better; the smallest region reaching ~0.05 is the per-mark cost.

READING
region needed:  5mC None   acetyl 40.0   acetyl+salt 40.0   phospho None   phospho+salt 20.0
THE PREDECLARED PREDICTION WAS BACKWARDS, AND THE DATA SAYS SO PLAINLY. I predicted the
steric mark would localise and the charge marks would not, reasoning from the ENERGY
result where a charge change had a non-convergent tail. The opposite happened: charge
marks converge and the neutral methyl does not.
THE REASON IS THE RATIO, NOT THE TAIL. What a region approximation must capture is the
LOCAL part of the response relative to the global part. A charge change drives a large
local deformation -- peak |u| of 1.7 to 3.4 A here -- so the local term dominates and a
finite region captures it. A methyl drives a peak of only 0.34 A, and the propagation
run already showed its displacement flattening rather than decaying, i.e. a floor of
whole-particle breathing. When the local response is that small, that floor is a LARGE
FRACTION of it, and no boundary-fixed region can reproduce a global mode.
So energy locality and structural locality are different properties and one does not
predict the other. That is the correction this run makes to the earlier reading.
SALT DECIDES THE CHARGE MARKS. Screened at 150 mM phosphorylation localises by 20 A; unscreened it does not converge in this sweep at all. So the cost of a
charge mark is set by whether the model includes screening -- a modelling choice, not
a fact about chromatin, and it must not be quoted as one.
CHROMOSOME ARITHMETIC, using the measured seconds-per-region above.
This is the cost of placing marks INDEPENDENTLY -- one local solve each. It is a floor, and
it is only the right number if marks do not interact; where two marks fall within one
region they need a joint solve and this understates them.
